vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: raai-business-analyst-pro
Version: 3.5.1

The bundle is a comprehensive business analytics toolset for the OpenClaw platform, providing structured templates and logic for financial reporting, unit economics, and investor-ready dashboards. The included shell scripts (install.sh, build.sh, and smoke-test.sh) perform standard file management, packaging, and local validation tasks without any evidence of malicious behavior, persistence, or unauthorized network activity. While the skill requests several API keys (e.g., Google Sheets, Telegram) in its metadata, these are consistent with its stated purpose of data integration and reporting, and the instructions in SKILL.md are focused entirely on legitimate business analysis logic.

llm.summary: The skill’s description and optional integrations match an analytics tool, but the package includes install/test scripts (not just prose) and asks you to populate a config with sensitive financial data — inspect those scripts and any network calls before running.

dimensions.detail: The name, description, SKILL.md and config.yaml all align: this is a CFO/business-analytics skill that asks the user to provide company/finance data and optionally integrate with model APIs, Sheets, Telegram or Supabase. Optional env vars (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_SHEETS_CREDENTIALS_JSON, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, SUPABASE_URL) are coherent with described integrations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions require filling config.yaml with potentially sensitive financial data and running provided scripts (install.sh, smoke-test.sh). That is expected for a local analytics skill, but it expands the agent's operations beyond pure prompt-only work (file I/O, local install). SKILL.md does not explicitly instruct sending data to external endpoints, but optional integrations would if the user supplies credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry claims no install spec (instruction-only) but the package actually contains install.sh and test/smoke-test.sh plus build.sh. build.sh appears benign (local packaging), but install.sh and smoke-test.sh contents were not shown in full here — any install/test script can modify user files or perform network I/O. Because the actual install script behavior is unknown, this raises risk and should be inspected before execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required secrets are declared. The optional environment variables are appropriate for the stated features (LLM models, Google Sheets integration, Telegram bot, Supabase). There is no unexplained request for unrelated credentials. However, providing those optional keys would enable networked behavior and potential data transmission to third parties.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and there are no declared config paths that grant cross-skill or system-level privileges. The README/install flow suggests copying into ~/.openclaw/skills which is a reasonable install location for a skill. Nothing indicates modification of other skills or forcing always-on presence.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package largely looks like the analytics skill it claims to be, but take these precautions before installing or running scripts: 1) Inspect install.sh and test/smoke-test.sh (open them in an editor) and search for network calls (curl, wget, nc, python requests), remote URLs, or commands that modify unrelated system files. 2) Run the installer and smoke-test in a disposable environment (VM, container, or throwaway account) if you can't fully verify the scripts. 3) Do not paste real API keys or financial data into config.yaml until you confirm where data is sent; optional env vars (OpenAI/Anthropic/Google Sheets/Telegram/Supabase) will enable outbound behavior. 4) Backup any files the installer might modify and prefer to run with least privilege. 5) If you want higher assurance, request the full contents of install.sh and smoke-test.sh and share them for a focused review — their contents determine whether this is safe to run on your machine.
